# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Build and Development Commands

All build, test and run commands are `make` targets — see `make help` and the `makefile`.
Simulator scheme and destination come from `IOS_SCHEME` / `IOS_DESTINATION` at the top of the
`makefile` (default: iPhone 17e, iOS 27.0 — the Xcode 27 toolchain does not run on older runtimes).

```bash
make init          # Generate Packages/ from scripts/init_*.sh and build (only when Packages/ is absent)
make build         # Format, gen, arch-check, xcodegen (local shared packages if present, else remote), build
make build-prod    # Format, arch-check, xcodegen (remote packages, FORCE_REMOTE_PACKAGES=1), build
make compile       # Compile only (no format/gen/xcodegen, Xcode Cmd+B equivalent)
make test          # UI smoke test + package tests (Database, Services, Main) in iOS Simulator
make run           # Build, install and launch in simulator
make format        # SwiftFormat on this repository only
make lint          # SwiftLint
make gen           # Project code generation (alternative icon previews); never writes to shared packages
make arch-check    # Fail on forbidden imports between layers (scripts/check_architecture.sh)
make init-scripts  # Regenerate scripts/init_*.sh from the current Packages/
make verify-init   # Fail if scripts/init_*.sh no longer reproduce Packages/
make clean         # Clean build/ and DerivedData
make review        # codex review of uncommitted changes; BASE=<branch> reviews the branch diff vs origin/<branch>
make up-build      # Increment build number and rebuild
make up-version    # Bump app version (patch/minor/major) and rebuild
```

### Local vs Remote Development
- Shared Oversize packages live in `$HOME/Developer/Packages` and are addressed by absolute path in
  `Configs/PackagesLocal.yml` and `sharedPackagesPath` in each `Package.swift` — worktrees need no symlink
- Local mode is used when that directory exists and `FORCE_REMOTE_PACKAGES` is not `1`
- `make build-prod` exports `FORCE_REMOTE_PACKAGES=1` to force remote resolution
- `___PACKAGENAME___.xcodeproj` is generated by XcodeGen and is not tracked in git: run `make build` after clone
  or after changing `Configs/*.yml`. Xcode Cloud generates it in `ci_scripts/ci_post_clone.sh`
- Tooling never modifies `$HOME/Developer/Packages`: those packages are shared between projects

## Architecture Overview

### Modular Structure (Swift Package Manager)
Five local packages in `Packages/`. Dependency graph (enforced by `make arch-check`):

```
App ──► Services ──► Database ──► Models
 │                                  ▲
 ├──────────────────────────────────┘
 └──► Env
```

1. **App** - Features, three library products (`Main`, `Onboarding`, `Settings`)
   - Depends on `Models`, `Services`, `Env`; never on `Database` or `SwiftData`
2. **Services** - App services: business logic, validation, notifications, network
   - `Services/` - `actor` services working only with Domain models
   - `Injection/` - Factory registrations (`Container.___VARIABLE_modelVariableName___Service`)
3. **Database** - Persistence
   - `Entities/` - `internal` SwiftData `@Model` entities
   - `Mapping/` - `internal` Entity ↔ Domain mapping
   - `Services/` - `@ModelActor` storage services returning Domain models
   - `Injection/` - `ModelContainer` and storage registrations
4. **Models** - Public Domain models (`___VARIABLE_modelName___`), no persistence types
5. **Env** - Leaf module shared by the app target and features
   - `Destinations/` - Navigation destination enums
   - `Tabs/` - `RootTabs` (in Env so features can switch tabs via `.navigationMove`)

### Navigation Architecture
**Adaptive UI pattern**: a single `TabView` in `___PACKAGENAME___/Root/RootView.swift` with
`.tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable)` and `.defaultAdaptableTabBarPlacement(.sidebar)`:
- **Compact**: bottom tab bar over `RootTabs.tabs`
- **Regular**: native sidebar with the same tabs (header "___PACKAGENAME___" via `.tabViewSidebarHeader`)
- The same view adapts in place, so tab stacks keep their state when the size class changes.
  Never switch `tabViewStyle` or root views with `if/else` on `horizontalSizeClass` — it recreates the tree
- `RootView` owns `selectedTab` (`@SceneStorage`, restored across launches), registers the **only**
  `RootTabs` receiver `.onNavigationReceive(assign: $selectedTab)` (NavigatorUI default `executionDelay`) and installs
  `.navigationRoot(navigator)`

**Basic navigation variant** (projects created with the Basic navigation option): there is no `TabView`.
`RootView` hosts a single `MainNavigationStack` and installs `.navigationRoot(navigator)`; `ResolveTabs.swift` does not
exist. Settings open from the gear button (`ToolbarItem(placement: .topBarLeading)`) in `MainNavigationStack` as a
sheet with `AppSettingsNavigationStack`, which is the only `AppSettingsDestinations` receiver. `RootTabs` stays in Env
and only provides the stack scene ids

**Navigation flow**:
1. `___PACKAGENAME___/App/___PACKAGENAME___App.swift` — only `@main`: `Launcher { RootView() }.onboarding { OnboardingNavigationStack() }`
2. `___PACKAGENAME___/Navigation/Tabs/ResolveTabs.swift` — `RootTabs: @retroactive View`, maps each tab to its stack
3. `___PACKAGENAME___/Navigation/Stacks/` — one `ManagedNavigationStack(scene: RootTabs.<tab>.id)` per tab
   (`MainNavigationStack`, `AppSettingsNavigationStack`) plus `OnboardingNavigationStack`, each with `.appEnvironment()`
4. `___PACKAGENAME___/Navigation/Destinations/` — `@retroactive NavigationDestination` conformances
5. Destination enums in `Packages/Env/Sources/Env/Destinations/` as plain `public nonisolated enum ...: Hashable, Sendable`

### Dependency Injection (Factory Kit)
ViewModels inject app services only:

```swift
@Injected(\.___VARIABLE_modelVariableName___Service) private var ___VARIABLE_modelVariableName___Service: ___VARIABLE_modelName___Service
```

- Services resolve storage with `@LazyInjected(\.storageService)`, so the `@ModelActor` is created
  inside the service actor rather than on the main actor during ViewModel init
- Registrations use `.cached` scope (container-bound, resettable in tests), not `.singleton`
- `modelContainerService` switches to an in-memory store via `.onPreview` / `.onTest`

### Data Layer (SwiftData)
- **Entities**: SwiftData `@Model`, `internal` to `Database`; Domain models live in `Models`
- **Storage services**: `@ModelActor`, API in Domain models, errors as `PersistenceError`
  (`itemNotFound` is preserved, not remapped to `fetchFailed`/`updateFailed`)
- **External storage**: Use `@Attribute(.externalStorage)` for images
- **CloudKit**: no `@Attribute(.unique)`; every property optional or with a default
- `ModelContainer` falls back from CloudKit to local storage before failing (`Database/Injection/Injection.swift`)
- The app never injects `.modelContainer(...)` into the environment: no `@Query` in App packages

### MVVM + Module Pattern
- **@Module macro** from OversizeArchitecture for feature modules
- **ViewStateProtocol** pattern for state management
- **Async/Await** throughout (Swift 6 strict concurrency enabled)
- **Actors** for shared mutable state

## Code Guidelines

### Swift 6 Concurrency
- Full strict concurrency checking enabled
- Use actors for services accessing shared state
- Prefer async/await over callbacks
- Mark @MainActor for UI-bound types
- `@ObservableDefaults` storage must be declared as
  `@MainActor @ObservableDefaults(ignoreExternalChanges: true) final class Storage: Sendable` —
  without `ignoreExternalChanges` the UserDefaults observer reenters AttributeGraph and crashes

### File Organization
- **New views**: Create in `Subviews/` folder within feature module
- **Previews**: Always include #Preview for SwiftUI views
- **Marks**: Use `// MARK: -` for section organization (English)
- **Comments**: Avoid unless necessary (code should be self-documenting)

### Module Pattern
```swift
@Module
public enum FeatureName: ModuleProtocol {}

@View(module: FeatureName.self)
public struct FeatureView: ViewProtocol {
    public var body: some View { ... }
}

@ViewModel(module: FeatureName.self)
public actor FeatureViewModel: ViewModelProtocol { ... }

@Observable
public final class FeatureViewState: ViewStateProtocol {
    public init(input _: FeatureName.Input?) {}
}
```

### Navigation Pattern
Destination enum in `Env`, free of any navigation framework:

```swift
public nonisolated enum FeatureDestinations: Hashable, Sendable {
    case detail(id: UUID)
    case settings
}
```

Conformance and mounting in the app target only:

```swift
extension FeatureDestinations: @retroactive NavigationDestination {
    @MainActor
    public var body: some View { ... }

    public var method: NavigationMethod { .push }
}

ManagedNavigationStack(scene: RootTabs.main.id) {
    Feature.buildCached()
        .navigationAutoReceive(FeatureDestinations.self)
}
.appEnvironment()
```

Screens set `viewState.destination` and apply `.navigationOpen($viewState.destination)` (local, in
the current stack). `.navigationMove(_:)` broadcasts across the whole tree and is reserved for global
intents (deep links, tab switching).

### NavigatorUI Import Rule
- `import NavigatorUI` is allowed **only** in the app target: `___PACKAGENAME___/Root/RootView.swift` and
  `___PACKAGENAME___/Navigation/`. Forbidden anywhere in `Packages/`, including previews and `@retroactive` conformances
- Screens navigate only through `OversizeNavigation` modifiers and `Navigation*Layout` views; if a
  behaviour is missing, it belongs in `OversizeNavigation`, not in the feature
- Exactly **one** `navigationAutoReceive` / `onNavigationReceive` per destination type in the whole
  tree — a second handler silently steals the value and navigation lands in the wrong stack
- Module view structs keep the `View` suffix (`OnboardingGreetingView`): the name must differ from the `@Module` enum
- The module enum file is `X.swift`, except `Main`: `Main.swift` is treated by SwiftPM as `main.swift`
  (case-insensitive file system) and turns the target into an executable, so it is `MainModule.swift`
- Feature modules are never named `*Root`: the root level lives only in `___PACKAGENAME___/App`, `___PACKAGENAME___/Root` and
  `___PACKAGENAME___/Navigation`. The only exception is `RootTabs` in `Env/Tabs`. A tab's first screen is named after the
  tab (`Main`, `AppSettings`)
- Screens with parameters (`___VARIABLE_modelName___Detail`) are built with `build(input:)`; `buildCached()` only
  for tab roots whose state should survive re-creation

## Key Files

- `___PACKAGENAME___/App/___PACKAGENAME___App.swift` - Main app entry
- `___PACKAGENAME___/Root/RootView.swift` - Root coordinator
- `___PACKAGENAME___/Navigation/Tabs/ResolveTabs.swift` - Tab → stack resolution
- `Packages/App/Sources/Main/` - Reference feature: `Main` (list) → `___VARIABLE_modelName___Detail`
- `Configs/Base.yml`, `Configs/Settings.yml`, `Configs/Targets.yml`, `Configs/Schemes.yml` - XcodeGen
- `Configs/Packages.yml` / `Configs/PackagesLocal.yml` - Remote / local dependencies
- `scripts/check_architecture.sh`, `scripts/generate_init_scripts.py`, `scripts/verify_init.sh` - Guards

## Build Configurations

Two configurations (`Configs/Base.yml`, `Configs/Settings.yml`, `Configs/Targets.yml`):
1. **Debug** — display name "___PACKAGENAME___ Dev", icon AppIcon(Dev), condition DEBUG
2. **AppStore** — display name "___PACKAGENAME___", icon AppIcon, condition APPSTORE

Bundle id is `___VARIABLE_bundleIdentifierPrefix:bundleIdentifier___.___PACKAGENAME___` in both. Schemes: "___PACKAGENAME___ (Dev)" and "___PACKAGENAME___ (AppStore)".

## Dependencies

Versions are defined in `Configs/Packages.yml` and in each `Packages/*/Package.swift` — keep them in sync.

- **Oversize**: OversizeUI, OversizeKit (Launcher, Settings, Onboarding, Notices), OversizeArchitecture
  (`@Module`), OversizeNavigation, OversizeServices, OversizeCore, OversizeLocalizable, OversizeResources
- **Third-party**: Factory (DI, `FactoryTesting` in tests), Navigator (`NavigatorUI`, app target only),
  ObservableDefaults

## Project Setup

After clone: `make build` (generates `___PACKAGENAME___.xcodeproj` and builds).

`make init` is for a fresh template checkout without `Packages/`: it runs `scripts/init_packages.sh`,
`init_packages_files.sh` and `init_packages_swiftdata_files.sh`, then `make build` and reopens Xcode.
`make init` also runs `scripts/init_app_tests.sh` (UI smoke test) before the build.
The init scripts are generated from this repository (`make init-scripts`) and must stay in sync
(`make verify-init`).

### Code Quality Tools
- **SwiftFormat**: Formats this repository (`make format`)
- **SwiftLint**: Opt-in rules enabled
- **XcodeGen**: Project generation from YAML configs
- **arch-check**: Forbidden imports between layers

## Tests

- Swift Testing in package test targets, run by `make test` through the scheme:
  `DatabaseTests` (storage on an in-memory container), `ServicesTests` and `MainTests`
  (`@Suite(.container)` from `FactoryTesting`, so every test gets a fresh container and in-memory store)
- `___PACKAGENAME___UITests` - launch smoke test
- ViewModels are tested directly: `XViewModel(state:input:output:)` + `handleAction(_:)`

## Development Workflow

1. Change code in this repository only; shared packages are read-only from here
2. `make build` (format, arch-check, xcodegen, build)
3. `make test` before PR
4. After changing anything in `Packages/`: `make init-scripts` and `make verify-init`
5. `make build-prod` to check remote package resolution

`.claude/team/WORKFLOW.md`, роль Team Lead — в `.claude/team/TEAM_LEAD.md`, инварианты — в
`.claude/team/rules/`. Запуск: `make team-run TASK="..."`, `make team-resume`, `make team-once`.
Перед первым запуском задать `PROJECT_NUMBER` (GitHub Project ___PACKAGENAME___) и id полей в `.claude/team/rules/GITHUB.md`.

Quality gates: Implementation → Build → Architecture Review → Code Review → Manual QA → Merge.
